title: HyperOnboard: Role Launch Snapshot and 30-90 Activation Template
content:
Purpose: quick, reusable working template to take a candidate through offer acceptance to contribution in 30/60/90 days. Combine a compact hiring plan, a measurable interview rubric, and a pragmatic onboarding checklist that managers and POs can copy-edit for specific roles.

Status and intent: working draft for FY26 hiring sprints (early trials with infra and platform-engineering hiring waves). This is intentionally opinionated about signals we care about (ramp speed, cross-team communication, test-driven ownership). Use as a baseline; annotate with role-specific tasks and replace TODOs.

Quick orientation (one-liner): HyperOnboard is a "launch packet"—a short, shareable checklist + rubric to align hiring, the hiring manager, mentor/buddy, and recruiting operations on acceptance -> day 90 outcomes.

Scope: ICs (IC2–IC5) across engineering, product, and SRE. Not a replacement for full People Ops handbook; intended to accelerate first-90 days and instrument early quality signals for hiring calibration.

Hiring plan snapshot (for manager + recruiter):
- Hiring signal: 2–3 concrete deliverables expected in first 90 days (choose 1 fast win in month 1, 1 impact work in month 2, 1 cross-team deliverable by month 3).
- Timeline: Week 0: offer & logistics; Week 1: shadow + infra access; Week 2–4: small shipable task; Month 2: feature/infra milestone; Month 3: cross-team rollout + owner handoff.
- Interview loop (baseline for eng roles): Recruit screen (30m) -> Hiring manager (45m) -> Two technical rounds (60m each: system design + code pairing) -> Collaboration/communication round (30–45m) -> Exec/skip-level if IC4+ (30m). Total on-site loop time 3.5–4.5 hours.
- Comms: recruiting to post-offer email should include role launch snapshot (this doc), buddy assignment, first-week calendar skeleton, and links to requisite access checklists.

Offer packet checklist (ops items to complete before start):
- Signed offer + I-9 (if applicable)
- Manager assigned, buddy assigned, and initial 1:1 scheduled for day 1
- Infra access requests issued (jira access + repo perms + cloud console)
- Workstation shipped or on-site booking confirmed
- Security & compliance onboarding assigned (if private deployment/regulatory customer)
- Prestart reading pack shared (team RFCs, relevant incidents, current PRs)

Interview rubric (single-page, numerical scale 1–5, with anchor examples). Use for calibration and debrief notes. Keep score fields in ATS but capture qualitative: examples, gaps, and evidence.
- Areas and anchors:
  - Technical correctness (1–5): Can the candidate implement correct, maintainable code during pairing and explain tradeoffs? Anchors: 5 = correct and robust solution with edge cases and tests; 3 = correct but brittle or missing edge cases; 1 = incorrect or major misconceptions.
  - System design (1–5): Ability to decompose requirements, propose measurable SLAs, identify bottlenecks, and consider operational costs. Anchors: 5 = clear architecture + failure modes + rollout plan; 2 = vague tradeoffs, misses core ops concerns.
  - Product sense & impact orientation (1–5): Prioritization, outcome-thinking, ability to tie technical choices to user/business impact. Anchors: 5 = identifies measurable metrics and tradeoffs; 1 = overly academic solutions with no product tie.
  - Collaboration & communication (1–5): Clarity of explanations, receptive to feedback, cross-functional mindset. Anchors: 5 = proactive clarifying, invites feedback; 2 = closed off or unclear.
  - Ownership & learning velocity (1–5): Evidence of shipping end-to-end, learning new domains quickly. Anchors: 5 = repeated examples of shipping and improving systems; 1 = no evidence of ownership.
  - Cultural/values fit (1–5): Evidence of glue work, candidate’s ability to operate in high-performance, ambiguous environments. Anchors: 5 = pragmatic, bias for action, clear examples; 1 = passive.
- Interview debrief template (copy into ATS notes): "Top strengths (2–3): ...
  Top risks (2–3): ...
  Required onboarding supports if hired: ...
  Recommended 30/60/90 milestones: ..."

Onboarding checklist (practical, manager-first):
- Pre-day-1 (recruiting + manager): welcome doc + first-week calendar sent; Slack invite; send buddy intro email; create required infra tickets; create first-ticket for fast-win task (estimate <3 days).
- Day 1: 1:1 with manager (30–60m) covering role context + 30/60/90 goals; team lunch (virtual/in-person); buddy walkthrough of repos and dev flow; confirm access to ticketing and CI.
- Day 2–5: environment setup validation (local dev, tests pass), complete required security trainings, pair on the fast-win task with buddy, first-week retrospective on Friday (30m).
- Week 2–4: ship fast-win (owner signs off), start second deliverable (mentor-guided), scheduled sync with adjacent team leads.
- Month 1 manager check (end of month): evidence review of fast-win, signal check on documentation contributions, feedback conversation and adjustments to 30/60/90.
- Month 2: take ownership of a mid-scale deliverable, lead a small design doc, participate in oncall rotation shadow if applicable.
- Month 3: lead cross-team rollout or ship major milestone; provide retrospective + proposal for ongoing ownership.

Manager checklist and risk mitigations:
- Before start: confirm buddy and first-ticket exist.
- Weekly 1:1 agenda template: 5m personal check-in, 10m blockers, 20m skill-building or project planning, 10m feedback loop.
- Escalation triggers (email to p-ops + hiring manager): not shipping a measurable artifact by day 30, ongoing access blockers >48h, repeated missing meetings.

Buddy playbook (short):
- First 2 weeks: pair 3x for 90–120m on dev flow and codebase.
- Provide curated list of 6–8 reading items (design docs, incidents, coding standards).
- Shadowing: 2 oncall tickets, 1 deploy cycle.

Evaluation signals (early):
- Technical: able to run test suite locally and fix one failing test in week 1.
- Product: articulates impact metric for a fast-win by end of week 1.
- Collaboration: schedules and leads at least one cross-team sync by week 4.
- Ownership: closes owner-assigned ticket with PR and reviewer responses in <2 weeks.

Template: 30/60/90 milestones (copyable):
- 30 days (learn & ship): complete environment, ship small bug/feature, present learnings to team.
- 60 days (own & expand): own a component or endpoint, reduce latency/bug rate or deliver feature scope, mentor newcomer pairing.
- 90 days (integrate & lead): lead a cross-team launch or own SLA for a subservice, propose roadmap items.

Recruiting playbook notes (ops & interviewer hints):
- Recruiter checklist: send role launch snapshot with offer email; collect candidate prestart constraints (visa, hardware needs); confirm buddy availability.
- Interviewers: focus on concrete examples. Ask for "past 2–3 months shipped work" and one code example. Rate on evidence, not potential.
- Calibration: every hiring round should include at least one calibrated interviewer (eng lead who has completed calibration exercise in last 6 months).

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Define explicit ramp metrics per org (platform vs. product eng) — who owns this? action: Priya to draft baseline by 2026-02-12.
- Should we require a documented 90-day plan in the offer packet for IC4+? pros/cons noted (clarity vs. inflexibility).
- Add a short checklist for Private deployments hires (HSM/KMS onboarding).

Sample email snippets (copyable):
- Pre-start welcome: "Congrats and welcome — attached is a short launch snapshot with your first-week calendar, your assigned buddy (NAME), and a link to our quick-start repo. Please complete the short security training before day 3."
- Manager day-1 note: "Hi NAME — excited to have you. Today we'll cover role context and your first-week goals. Please bring questions about accounts/access. Expect a walking tour of current work and an intro to the fast-win ticket."

Notes-to-self / working artifacts:
- Keep this doc <2 pages for offer attachments. Expanded examples belong in Role Launch Library (linked_artifacts).
- Run a pilot with 6 hires in Q1 2026 and collect manager/buddy NPS at day 30 and day 90.

Version history: 0.1 draft — initial template compiled from hiring interviews, manager feedback, and recent onboarding retros (nov 2025–feb 2026).

Appendix (quick checklist for recruiter to paste into ATS notes):
- OfferStatus: signed/unsigned
- BuddyAssigned: yes/no
- FirstTicketCreated: ticket-id
- WorkstationShipped: yes/no
- SecurityTrainingAssigned: yes/no

End of HyperOnboard template. Copy, edit, and iterate.
